hero.tagline: The A-Town Welcome Is Like No Other
hero.description: Atlanta brings the 2026 tournament to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, one of the most architecturally striking venues in North American sports. ATL's world-class dining scene, legendary music culture, and legendary Southern hospitality make it one of the most exciting host cities in the draw. Expect full-throated crowds and unforgettable nights.

stadium.name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
stadium.transport: Mercedes-Benz Stadium sits in downtown Atlanta with excellent MARTA access. Take MARTA Red or Gold Line to Five Points, transfer to the Green or Blue Line to Vine City station — a short walk to the stadium. From Hartsfield-Jackson Airport, MARTA Gold Line reaches Downtown in about 20 minutes.

quick_facts.matches_hosted: Multiple matches including group stage and advanced rounds
quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Major fan hub expected at Centennial Olympic Park adjacent to the stadium

weather.june: Hot and humid, highs around 29–32°C (84–90°F). Afternoon thunderstorms are common.
weather.july: Very hot and humid, highs 31–34°C (88–93°F). The stadium's retractable roof controls match-day weather.
packing_tips: Light, breathable fabrics — humidity in Atlanta in summer is real
A light rain jacket for afternoon storms
Sunscreen and a hat for outdoor fan zones
The stadium interior is heavily air-conditioned — bring a layer if you run cold

airports.name: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport
transfer_options: MARTA Gold Line: Airport to Five Points station in about 20 minutes — best option
Transfer at Five Points to Green/Blue Line for Vine City (stadium) station
Rideshare from ATL to Downtown or Midtown takes 20–35 minutes depending on traffic
Taxis available at ground transportation level
airports.notes: One of the world's busiest airports with outstanding MARTA rail connections to Downtown. The MARTA ride is the fastest and most affordable way into the city — much better than fighting traffic.

match_schedule.teams_or_placeholder: Mercedes-Benz Stadium hosts multiple matches. Full schedule after group draw.

public_transit: MARTA Green/Blue Line: Vine City station — 5-minute walk to Mercedes-Benz Stadium main gate
MARTA Red/Gold Line from Airport to Five Points, transfer to Green/Blue Line
Georgia State station also walkable for some entrances
rideshare: Rideshare to the stadium is practical but post-match surge is severe
Walk 3–4 blocks south on Northside Drive for a faster rideshare pickup
Pre-book scheduled rides before the match for better pricing
driving_parking: State Farm Arena and downtown lots are pre-bookable — do so well in advance
I-285 and I-75/85 connector can grid-lock for hours after big matches
Parking in Vine City or English Avenue neighbourhoods costs less but requires a longer walk
walking_biking: Centennial Olympic Park and Pemberton Place are walkable from Midtown hotels
BeltLine connects Midtown, Inman Park, and other neighbourhoods — not a direct route to the stadium but useful for non-match days
Limited secure bike parking near the stadium
match_day_tips: MARTA is the best choice — parking is brutal after sold-out matches
The stadium retractable roof will likely be closed in Atlanta July heat
Centennial Olympic Park fan area opens hours before kickoff — a great warm-up spot
Traffic on the Downtown Connector (I-75/85) is chaotic during and after games

fan_hubs.name: Centennial Olympic Park Fan Hub
fan_hubs.location: Centennial Olympic Park, 265 Park Ave W NW, Atlanta
fan_hubs.description: Atlanta's landmark Olympic park is adjacent to Mercedes-Benz Stadium and is expected to be the primary fan gathering area — giant screens, live entertainment, Atlanta's legendary food scene on display, and the symbolic backdrop of the 1996 Games.
transport_tips: MARTA Green/Blue Line to Vine City or Georgia State, then walk through the park
Walking distance from Downtown and CNN Center hotels
Arrive 2+ hours early for the best viewing spots on big match days

neighborhoods.name: Downtown
neighborhoods.best_for: Stadium proximity, fan hub access, business hotels
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Downtown core near CNN Center and Centennial Olympic Park is safe and well-patrolled. Avoid isolated side streets late at night.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: 5-minute walk or one MARTA stop to Mercedes-Benz Stadium
neighborhoods.description: Most convenient neighbourhood for both the stadium and the expected Centennial Olympic Park fan hub. Omni and Glenn hotels are a short walk from the gates. Great for fans who want to maximise match-day logistics.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe, active pedestrian area around Peachtree and 10th St.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: MARTA Red/Gold Line from Midtown station to Five Points, then Green/Blue — about 20 min
neighborhoods.description: A more vibrant alternative to Downtown. High Museum, Piedmont Park, and excellent restaurant options on Peachtree St. Good MARTA connections to the stadium.

neighborhoods.name: Buckhead
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe and upscale in the Buckhead Village area. Active late-night strip.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: MARTA Gold Line from Buckhead station to Five Points, transfer to Green/Blue — about 30 min
neighborhoods.description: Atlanta's luxury neighbourhood. The Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, and other flagship hotels. Excellent cocktail bars and upscale dining. Fado Irish Pub here is a top soccer destination.

neighborhoods.name: Old Fourth Ward / Inman Park
neighborhoods.best_for: Hip restaurants, BeltLine access, local culture
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Gentrifying area — generally safe on main corridors, aware at night in transitional blocks.
neighborhoods.description: Atlanta's most interesting neighbourhood for food and nightlife. The BeltLine trail, Ponce City Market, and some of the best restaurants in the city. Great for fans who want the local Atlanta experience.

hotels.name: Omni Atlanta Hotel at CNN Center
hotels.best_for: Stadium proximity, CNN Center access, large groups

hotels.name: The Glenn Hotel, Autograph Collection
hotels.best_for: Boutique luxury, rooftop bar, Downtown location

hotels.name: Four Seasons Atlanta
hotels.best_for: Luxury, spa, Midtown arts and dining access

bars.name: Stats Brewpub
bars.notes: Atlanta's premier soccer bar — multiple large screens, dedicated soccer programming, and a serious football crowd.
bars.transit: MARTA Green/Blue Line to Vine City or CNN Center

bars.name: Fado Irish Pub Atlanta
bars.notes: Authentic Irish pub in Buckhead with packed crowds for every major match. Arrive early.

bars.name: Park Bar Atlanta
bars.notes: Outdoor bar adjacent to Freedom Park near the BeltLine. Relaxed crowd, great for afternoon matches.

bars.name: Ladybird Grove & Mess Hall
bars.address: 684 John Wesley Dobbs Ave NE, Atlanta, GA
bars.notes: Outdoor patio bar on the BeltLine with food trucks and a festive atmosphere on big match days.

bars.name: SweetWater Brewing Company
bars.address: 1800 NE Expressway Access Rd, Atlanta, GA
bars.notes: Atlanta's most famous craft brewery with outdoor spaces and match screenings. Very local crowd.

transport.summary: Atlanta has MARTA rail and bus service connecting Hartsfield-Jackson Airport, Downtown, Midtown, and Buckhead. The stadium is a short walk from Vine City station. MARTA is the smart choice for match days.
tips: Get a MARTA Breeze card at the airport — reloadable and accepted on all rail and bus
Vine City station (Green/Blue Line) is the closest stop to Mercedes-Benz Stadium
Airport to Five Points is 20 minutes on MARTA Gold Line — do not take a cab for this trip
Rideshare surge after matches is extreme — use MARTA home or wait 30+ minutes before requesting
The BeltLine trail connects Old Fourth Ward, Midtown, and other neighbourhoods for daytime exploration

fan_zones.name: Centennial Olympic Park Fan Hub
fan_zones.location: Centennial Olympic Park, 265 Park Ave W NW
fan_zones.description: Adjacent to Mercedes-Benz Stadium — the primary fan hub area with giant screens, live music, and Atlanta's famous food scene. Site of the 1996 Olympics.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Atlanta United FC joined MLS in 2017 and immediately became one of the most successful clubs in league history, setting MLS attendance records and winning the 2018 MLS Cup. The Five Stripes fanbase is passionate, young, and one of the loudest in the league.

tourist_hits.name: Georgia Aquarium
tourist_hits.notes: World's largest aquarium — right next to Centennial Olympic Park. Book tickets in advance.

tourist_hits.name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
tourist_hits.notes: Powerful museum on civil rights history — one of the best museums in the South.

tourist_hits.name: World of Coca-Cola
tourist_hits.notes: Unique Atlanta attraction — the history and global reach of the world's most recognized brand.

tourist_hits.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Historic Site
tourist_hits.notes: Birth home and church of MLK Jr. in Sweet Auburn neighbourhood. Free admission.

local_favorites.name: Ponce City Market
local_favorites.notes: Converted Sears building in Old Fourth Ward — food hall, shops, and rooftop games.

local_favorites.name: Atlanta BeltLine
local_favorites.notes: 22-mile trail loop connecting neighborhoods. Rent a bike or e-scooter for a full loop.

local_favorites.name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
local_favorites.notes: Historic indoor market with diverse food vendors — the oldest continuously operating market in the South.

areas: Old Fourth Ward / Inman Park — Ponce City Market, best restaurants, BeltLine access
Midtown — Peachtree St restaurants, cocktail bars
Buckhead — upscale dining and late-night bars
Downtown / Castleberry Hill — pre-match bars near the stadium

recommendations.name: Staplehouse
recommendations.notes: One of the best restaurants in the South. Book months in advance.

recommendations.name: Gunshow
recommendations.notes: Dim sum-style Southern food by Kevin Gillespie. Unique and excellent.

recommendations.name: Mary Mac's Tea Room
recommendations.notes: Classic Atlanta institution for Southern comfort food since 1945.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Non-emergency Atlanta Police: (404) 614-6544. Hospital: Grady Memorial Hospital, (404) 616-1000.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Downtown, Midtown, and Old Fourth Ward are increasingly walkable. The BeltLine trail is transforming connectivity between neighborhoods.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: The BeltLine is excellent for cycling. Spin and Lime scooters operate throughout the city.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: Relay Bikeshare and e-scooter operators (Lime, Spin) operate in Atlanta. Best used along the BeltLine trail.

pickup_soccer.name: Piedmont Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Informal pickup on the large grass areas, especially on weekends. Mixed skill, diverse crowd.

pickup_soccer.name: Grant Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: Southeast Atlanta park with open fields and informal soccer, particularly among Latino community groups.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Stone Mountain Park
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Large state park with a walk-up trail to the massive granite outcrop. Laser light shows at night in summer.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Chattahoochee River Tubing
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Float the Chattahoochee in a tube — the classic Atlanta summer activity. Equipment rentals available at the put-in points.

safety_tips: Atlanta is a large city — tourist areas (Downtown near CNN/stadium, Midtown, Buckhead) are safe and well-patrolled
Use MARTA or rideshare for late-night travel — avoid walking in unfamiliar areas after midnight
The stadium area around Centennial Olympic Park is heavily managed on match days
Atlanta summer heat is serious — stay hydrated and take indoor breaks during peak afternoon heat
Lock any valuables in your hotel safe and avoid displaying expensive items in crowded fan zones
